speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your cough and how long you have been experiencing it? Do you produce any sputum, and if so, what color is it?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of recurrent sinus infections or nasal polyps, and do you experience shortness of breath or wheezing? I will also need to review your previous chest imaging and sputum culture results. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_High_Resolution

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal CT scan, I must consider conditions that cause chronic purulent sputum without structural lung damage, such as Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia or localized bronchiectasis missed on standard imaging. Have you experienced any ear infections, hearing loss, or a reversed arrangement of internal organs (situs inversus) in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience nasal congestion, chronic sinusitis, or nasal polyps? I also need to know if you have a history of recurrent ear infections or hearing loss. REQUEST TEST: Sweat_Cl_Test

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the sweat test and CT scan are normal, ruling out cystic fibrosis and typical structural bronchiectasis, I need to investigate other causes of chronic suppurative lung disease. Do you have a history of allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis (ABPA) or chronic sinusitis with nasal polyps? REQUEST TEST: Total_IgE_Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal workup for CF and ABPA, I need to rule out immunodeficiency or post-nasal drip. Do you have a history of recurrent sinusitis, nasal polyps, or frequent ear infections? REQUEST TEST: Serum_IgG_IgA_IgM

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal immunoglobulins, cystic fibrosis, and ABPA ruled out, I suspect Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia or a similar ciliary defect. Do you have a history of recurrent sinusitis, nasal polyps, or chronic otitis media? REQUEST TEST: Nasal_Nitric_Oxide_Level

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: RESULTS: Nasal Nitric Oxide Level: Significantly reduced (< 200 nL/min)

speaker: Doctor
text: The significantly reduced nasal nitric oxide level strongly supports a diagnosis of Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia. Do you have a history of recurrent ear infections or hearing loss, and have you ever been told you have situs inversus?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No other significant past medical history aside from the recurrent bronchitis. Social history: Non-smoker, no history of alcohol or drug abuse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming your medical history. I have enough information to proceed. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia
